gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: I ___ getting up early because I have done it for years.
gaps.hint: be used to means present familiarity
gaps.explanation: 'Be used to' plus -ing means familiarity with something, here in the present: am used to.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.

gaps.sentence: Listen! Someone ___ the violin in the flat above us.
gaps.hint: Listen signals an action happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Listen!' points to an action in progress at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is used: is playing.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.

gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
gaps.hint: a timeless scientific fact takes present simple
gaps.explanation: General truths and scientific facts take the present simple: boils.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.
